title: Memory write is half the loop — read-and-apply discipline is the other half
body: Saving to memory and writing signals is only useful if the reading side is equally disciplined. The gap: an agent can save a feedback entry, then open the next session with the same bad impulse because MEMORY.md is loaded but not meaningfully acted on. The fix-impulse overrides the framing in the moment. Historian watching tracks helps but only if historian review is triggered and its output is acted on. This is a framing and protocol design problem: wakeup loads MEMORY.md but there is no enforcement that behavioral feedback entries actually shape in-session decisions. The loop is: write → load → apply. Currently strong on write, partial on load, weak on apply. The protocol needs a mechanism that closes the apply step — not just surfaces the memory but ties it to in-session behavior checks.
